name: Need for Speed AI Trend: Your Car in the Movie Scene
blurb: The Need for Speed AI trend puts a photo of your own car or truck into a car-movie street scene: it cruises through a small town, spins burnouts in a cloud of tire smoke while people stare from a patio, and drives off.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 14 s, 720p, 9:16, sound off. The video prompt
prompts.text:
Only replace the main foreground vehicle with the vehicle from [Image 1]. Keep everything else in the video completely unchanged: original camera movement, shot composition, driving motion, speed, road, background, other cars, lighting, shadows, reflections, film grain, scene and action. Do not change anything else.

Recreate the reference video [Video 1] shot for shot: a cinematic movie-style street scene on a sunny day in a small American town, filmed like a car movie with black bars at the top and the bottom, with the same camera angles, cuts, timing and moves. The ONLY change: the hero vehicle of [Video 1], the red car with the low two-door body and the truck-like front, is now the vehicle in [Image 1], in EVERY shot.

THE VEHICLE = the vehicle in [Image 1], in EVERY shot, from the front, the side and behind, through a windshield and inside the smoke: copy it exactly (body shape and proportions, number of doors, cab, bed or trunk, paint color and finish, wheels and rims, lights, grille, ride height, bumpers, racks, light bars, tow gear or work body and every other part), whatever kind it is (car, pickup, SUV, van or work truck), so its owner knows it at once. A pickup keeps its own cab and bed; a four-door keeps four doors.
PAINT: the exact hue of [Image 1] in the sunny daylight of [Video 1]. If [Image 1] was taken at night or under colored lights, show the same paint as in daylight: a gold car stays gold, a dark car stays dark. Never grey, silver or white unless [Image 1] shows that color.
It drives the same path, speed and distance from the camera as the red car in [Video 1], faces the same way in every shot and does the same burnouts and slides. Take ONLY the vehicle from [Image 1]: never its background, ground, buildings, sky, night, light or people. Every shot, also the first frame, is the sunny town of [Video 1].

NEVER the red car of [Video 1]: NO red paint unless [Image 1] shows it, never its low two-door body or truck grille, never a generic sports car, never a mix of the two. The RED PICKUP TRUCK in the background (far right in shot 2, behind the vehicle in shot 3, parked on the right in shot 7) is a background car: it stays exactly as it is and never becomes the vehicle from [Image 1].

Shot 1 [0-1.3 s]: the vehicle rolls slowly past a lawn and a low wall, seen from the side, then from behind as it pulls away.
Shot 2 [1.3-2.3 s]: hard cut, from inside a following car, through its windshield: the vehicle comes TOWARD the camera on the left of the road, we see its FRONT; the SAME vehicle from [Image 1], never the red car.
Shot 3 [2.3-3.0 s]: hard cut, through the side window: the vehicle passes close beside, its hood and side fill the right of the frame; the SAME vehicle from [Image 1].
Shot 4 [3.0-4.7 s]: quick cuts from inside the following car, past its driver's dark silhouette: the vehicle drives ahead in light traffic, its REAR and tail lights to the camera.
Shot 5 [4.7-9.3 s]: hard cut: the vehicle spins burnouts in a wide intersection by a restaurant, thick white tire smoke from the rear wheels, sliding sideways; the camera follows it.
Shot 6 [9.3-12.5 s]: hard cut to the restaurant patio: adults at the railing turn and watch while the vehicle slides past behind them in its smoke.
Shot 7 [12.5-14 s]: hard cut, from behind: the vehicle rolls out of the parking lot toward the street, its REAR to the camera.

Keep the black bars at the top and the bottom of the frame. The onlookers stay as in [Video 1] and never take anything from [Image 1]. No dialogue throughout the entire video. No background music. Exactly one vehicle looks like [Image 1]. No badges, emblems, brand names or lettering on the vehicle, no readable number plate, no text, no captions, no logos, no watermark.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 10 s, 720p, 9:16, sound off. The video prompt
prompts.text:
Theme: street-racing-game-style police pursuit. Scene concept: Begin with cinematic nighttime shots of the vehicle from [Image 1]. Build up with a deep, aggressive V8 engine startup and revving. Transition into a high-speed nighttime street pursuit. Multiple police cruisers chasing closely behind with flashing red and blue lights. Realistic tire smoke, exhaust effects, motion blur, and cinematic camera angles. Important: the vehicle retains its actual appearance, body style, paint color, headlights, and modifications from [Image 1]. Do not replace it with a generic sports car.

THE VEHICLE = the vehicle in [Image 1], in EVERY shot: copy it exactly from [Image 1] (the body shape and proportions, the cab, bed or trunk, the paint color and finish, the wheels and rims, the lights, the grille shape, the lift or ride height, the bumpers, racks, light bars and every other part it has), whatever kind it is (a car, a pickup truck, an SUV or a van), so its owner knows it at once. The same vehicle from the first frame to the last: never a different or generic model. Take only the vehicle from [Image 1], not its background, its people or its daylight: it is night. If [Image 1] shows people, leave them out.

Shot 1 [0-2 s]: night, a low close shot of the parked vehicle under a street light; its headlights come on and the exhaust shakes as the engine revs.
Shot 2 [2-4 s]: hard cut, a low tracking shot beside it as it launches down a wet city street, the rear tires smoking.
Shot 3 [4-7 s]: hard cut, a wide shot from behind: it races down a highway at full speed with three police cruisers close behind, red and blue lights flashing, motion blur on the street lights.
Shot 4 [7-10 s]: hard cut, a low front three-quarter shot: it drifts through a corner in thick tire smoke and speeds away from the cruisers toward the camera.

Polished color grading and realistic visual effects, vertical 9:16. Plain police cruisers with no lettering, no badges and no agency names. No crash, no people hurt. No dialogue throughout the entire video. No background music. No badges, emblems, brand names or lettering on the vehicle, no readable number plate, no text, no captions, no logos, no watermark.
